correctness.rationale: Every 2-plane admits an orthonormal basis with mutually orthogonal horizontal components and mutually orthogonal central components. For the four-dimensional horizontal module of the seven-dimensional quaternionic Heisenberg H-type algebra, orthogonal horizontal vectors satisfy |[X,Y]|^2=|X|^2|Y|^2. Substitution in the published sectional-curvature formula gives the exact upper envelope F(p,q). Writing u=sqrt(pq) and v=sqrt((1-p)(1-q)) reduces 4F to 1-4u^2-v^2+6uv with u+v<=1. A two-case concave-quadratic maximization proves F<=4/11 and forces p=q=4/11 at equality. The only remaining inequalities are two unit-vector inner-product bounds, whose equality conditions are exactly the two stated j-alignment identities. The converse is immediate by substitution, and the source's exhibited plane satisfies the conditions.
